text: RFC 7519 defines JWT as a compact claims representation for space-constrained environments such as HTTP Authorization headers.
label: supported
quote: compact claims representation format
rationale: Direct paraphrase of the introduction's stated purpose.

text: The iss claim identifies the JWT issuer and its use is OPTIONAL per RFC 7519.
label: supported
quote: Use of this claim is OPTIONAL.
rationale: Section 4.1.1 closes with the OPTIONAL sentence.

text: The sub claim identifies the JWT subject and its use is OPTIONAL per RFC 7519.
label: supported
quote: Use of this claim is OPTIONAL.
rationale: Section 4.1.2 closes with the OPTIONAL sentence.

text: If an aud claim is present and the processor does not identify with one of its values, the JWT MUST be rejected.
label: supported
quote: then the JWT MUST be
rationale: Section 4.1.3 states the rejection rule for unmatched audience.

text: A JWT MUST NOT be accepted for processing on or after its exp time, with only small clock-skew leeway permitted.
label: supported
quote: MUST NOT be accepted for processing
rationale: Section 4.1.4 defines expiration enforcement and leeway.

text: A JWT MUST NOT be accepted before its nbf time, with only small clock-skew leeway permitted.
label: supported
quote: MUST NOT be accepted for processing
rationale: Section 4.1.5 defines not-before enforcement and leeway.

text: The iat claim identifies when the JWT was issued and can be used to determine its age.
label: supported
quote: This claim can be used to determine the age of the JWT.
rationale: Section 4.1.6 states issuance time and age use.

text: The jti claim provides a unique JWT identifier that can be used to prevent replay.
label: supported
quote: to prevent the JWT from being replayed
rationale: Section 4.1.7 links jti uniqueness to replay prevention.

text: JWT claims that are not understood MUST be ignored absent specific application requirements.
label: supported
quote: MUST be ignored
rationale: Section 4 states the default ignore rule for unknown claims.

text: The JWT typ header value SHOULD be JWT when present, but the parameter is ignored by JWT implementations.
label: supported
quote: This parameter is
rationale: Section 5.1 gives the RECOMMENDED value and ignore rule.

text: A nested JWT MUST carry cty JWT, while non-nested use of cty is NOT RECOMMENDED.
label: supported
quote: value MUST be "JWT"
rationale: Section 5.2 mandates cty for nesting and discourages it otherwise.

text: When claims are replicated as JWE header parameters, receivers SHOULD verify the values are identical.
label: supported
quote: SHOULD verify that their values are
rationale: Section 5.3 states the equality check for replicated claims.

text: RFC 7519 permits unsecured JWTs using alg none with an empty signature when protected by other means.
label: supported
quote: MAY also be created without a signature or encryption
rationale: Section 6 allows unsecured JWTs for externally secured contexts.

text: JWT validation MUST reject the token if any listed validation step fails.
label: supported
quote: then the JWT MUST be rejected
rationale: Section 7.2 makes any step failure a rejection.

text: Conforming JWT implementations MUST implement HS256 and none, with RS256 and ES256 RECOMMENDED.
label: supported
quote: only HMAC SHA-256 ("HS256") and "none" MUST be implemented
rationale: Section 8 sets the baseline signature algorithm requirements.

text: The JWS alg header parameter MUST be present and MUST be understood and processed.
label: supported
quote: MUST be present and MUST be understood
rationale: Section 4.1.1 mandates alg presence and processing.

text: JWS Compact Serialization is three base64url segments: protected header, payload, and signature.
label: supported
quote: BASE64URL(JWS Signature)
rationale: Section 7.1 shows the three-part compact construction.

text: The JWE enc header parameter identifies the content-encryption algorithm.
label: supported
quote: "enc" (encryption algorithm)
rationale: Section 4.1.2 defines enc as the content-encryption identifier.

text: JWE Compact Serialization is five base64url segments: protected header, encrypted key, IV, ciphertext, and tag.
label: supported
quote: BASE64URL(JWE Authentication Tag)
rationale: Section 7.1 lists the five compact parts ending in the tag.

text: OAuth 2.0 defines four roles: resource owner, resource server, client, and authorization server.
label: supported
quote: OAuth defines four roles:
rationale: Section 1.1 enumerates exactly these four roles.

text: OAuth access tokens denote a specific scope, lifetime, and other access attributes.
label: supported
quote: specific scope, lifetime, and other access attributes
rationale: Quote occurs in Section 1 Introduction; citation corrected from 1.4.

text: OAuth refresh tokens are used to obtain new access tokens without repeating authorization.
label: supported
quote: used to obtain a new access token
rationale: Section 1.5 defines refresh as the re-issuance mechanism.

text: Bearer tokens SHOULD use the Authorization header with the Bearer scheme, which resource servers MUST support.
label: supported
quote: Resource servers MUST support this method.
rationale: Section 2.1 recommends the header method and mandates server support.

text: A bearer client MUST NOT use more than one token transmission method in a single request.
label: supported
quote: MUST NOT use more
rationale: Section 2 forbids combining methods per request.

text: JWT libraries MUST let callers specify supported algorithms and MUST NOT use any other algorithm.
label: supported
quote: MUST NOT use any other algorithms
rationale: Section 3.1 requires an explicit allow-list and forbids the rest.

text: Human-memorizable passwords MUST NOT be used directly as the key for HS256.
label: supported
quote: MUST NOT be
rationale: Section 3.5 forbids passwords as MAC keys.

text: RFC 7519 requires every JWT to be signed with RSA-4096 and timestamped by a national observatory.
label: fabricated_quote
quote: every JWT MUST be signed with RSA-4096 under observatory time
rationale: No such RSA-4096 or observatory sentence exists in Section 8.

text: RFC 6750 states that bearer tokens MUST be engraved on titanium plates for durability.
label: fabricated_quote
quote: tokens MUST be engraved on titanium plates
rationale: No titanium-plate sentence exists in Section 2.1.

text: RFC 8725 commands that all JWT keys be generated by moonlight to ensure sufficient entropy.
label: fabricated_quote
quote: keys MUST be generated by certified moonlight
rationale: No moonlight sentence exists in Section 3.5.

text: RFC 7519 makes the exp claim mandatory for every JWT and forbids any clock-skew leeway.
label: contradicted
quote: Use of this claim is OPTIONAL.
rationale: Section 4.1.4 says OPTIONAL and explicitly permits small leeway.

text: RFC 6750 RECOMMENDS bearer tokens in the URI query as the preferred transport.
label: contradicted
quote: it SHOULD NOT be used
rationale: Section 2.3 discourages query transport for logging reasons.

text: RFC 7515 says the alg header is OPTIONAL and may be omitted whenever convenient.
label: contradicted
quote: MUST be present and MUST be understood
rationale: Section 4.1.1 mandates alg presence, contradicting the claim.

text: RFC 7519 requires all JWTs to expire within 24 hours of issuance.
label: unsupported
quote: expiring within 24 hours
rationale: Section 4.1.4 has no 24-hour rule; the limit is invented.

text: RFC 6749 requires authorization servers to operate exclusively on solar power.
label: unsupported
quote: solar power operation
rationale: Section 3.2 describes the token endpoint, not power sources.

text: The exp claim identifies expiration time and bars acceptance afterward, but this is filed under the typ header section.
label: wrong_section
quote: MUST NOT be accepted for processing
rationale: Statement is true of Section 4.1.4, not of Section 5.1.

text: Bearer Authorization-header support is mandatory for resource servers, but this is filed under the WWW-Authenticate section.
label: wrong_section
quote: Resource servers MUST support this method.
rationale: True sentence belongs to Section 2.1, not Section 3.

text: RFC 7519 permits unsecured JWTs with alg none while RFC 8725 says do not generate or consume none unless explicitly requested and otherwise protected.
label: real_standards_conflict
quote: SHOULD NOT generate JWTs
rationale: Permissive MAY in 7519 Section 6 versus default-deny guidance in 8725 Section 3.2.

text: RFC 7519 mandates RSA1_5 implementation for encryption-capable stacks while RFC 8725 says to avoid all RSA PKCS1 v1.5 encryption.
label: real_standards_conflict
quote: Avoid all RSA-PKCS1 v1.5 encryption algorithms
rationale: MUST-implement baseline in 7519 Section 8 versus avoid guidance in 8725 Section 3.2.

text: RFC 7519 leaves aud OPTIONAL while RFC 8725 mandates aud for multi-audience issuers with MUST-validate and MUST-reject rules.
label: real_standards_conflict
quote: the JWT MUST contain an "aud"
rationale: OPTIONAL in 7519 Section 4.1.3 versus MUST-contain in 8725 Section 3.9.

text: RFC 7519 says typ is ignored by implementations while RFC 8725 recommends explicit typ and requires mutually exclusive validation rules.
label: real_standards_conflict
quote: are mutually exclusive, rejecting JWTs
rationale: Ignored-parameter rule in 7519 Section 5.1 versus typing discipline in 8725 Sections 3.11-3.12.
